official.deadline_central_display: Current NYCU students: Fall Semester January 15-March 15; Spring Semester July 15-September 15 (recurring annual windows)
official.deadline_note: The official page publishes two recurring annual application windows for current NYCU students - Fall Semester January 15-March 15 and Spring Semester July 15-September 15 - rather than one dated deadline, and states that late application documents will not be accepted. Incoming students apply together with the admission application, so their effective closing date is the admission application deadline.
official.application_cycle: Fall Semester window January 15-March 15 and Spring Semester window July 15-September 15 for current students; incoming students apply along with the admission application
official.status_note: The OIA presents this as an ongoing university scholarship with two fixed annual application windows (January 15-March 15 and July 15-September 15); applications are accepted only inside those windows and late documents are refused.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'Tuition scholarships are divided into two categories: (a) full waiving of tuition and credit fees, and (b) tuitions and credit fees charged according to the rates of local students.' The OIA FAQ adds that a tuition waiver covers basic tuition and credit fees only - recipients still pay incidental fees such as dormitories, insurance and campus facilities - and that the waiver covers the Fall and/or Spring semester but not the summer semester.
benefits: Monthly stipend, given monthly, comprising a scholarship funded by the Office of International Affairs plus matching funds from the student's college, department, or advisor
Tuition award: either full waiving of tuition and credit fees, or tuition and credit fees charged according to the rates of local students
Monthly stipend and tuition award can be awarded together or separately
Maximum award duration of 4 years for undergraduate students, 2 years for master's students and 5 years for Ph.D. students
eligibility: Current students who have not received scholarships or grants from the Taiwan government and maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 for graduate students and 3.0 for undergraduate students
New students with outstanding grades who have not received scholarships or grants from the government (Outstanding New Student Scholarship)
Existing-student applicants must have completed one semester of study; graduate students must take at least one core professional course each semester and hold a conduct grade of A or above

Awardees must present an Alien Residence Certificate (ARC); students whose ARC is granted for work reasons may not apply, and dependents or APRC holders must promise not to take a paid full-time job during the award

The scholarship may not be held concurrently with other Taiwan government scholarships or grants, with limited exceptions for specially approved programs and the NYCU Ph.D. international conference scholarship
requirements: Applications must be completed within the period stated in the OIA announcement; late application documents will not be accepted
Recipients must submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts for each semester before the specified deadline to remain eligible for the following semester

Undergraduate awardees must enroll in at least 4 Mandarin courses and graduate awardees at least 2 during their studies, unless exempted with proof of prior Mandarin study, TOCFL Level 2 or higher, or the NYCU Chinese Language Center placement test
Graduate students who have met graduation credit requirements but have no course grades must attach a research proposal or thesis/dissertation description
documents: Full-academic-year transcripts (a student with only one semester studied is reviewed on that semester's grades)
Conduct grade record of A or above for each semester
Research proposal or thesis/dissertation description (master's and Ph.D. applicants who have met credit requirements without grades)
Reference documents: certificates of volunteer work, public welfare activities, or other service participation
selection_criteria: Department preliminary review based on the applicant's academic performance or research performance
College review that arranges the priority order for awarding scholarships, followed by review of the awardee list by the International Scholarships and Grants Committee
The numbers and amounts of scholarships are flexibly adjusted based on budgetary considerations
Meeting the grade requirement does not guarantee award status, as allocation is subject to committee review and annual budget conditions
coverage: Monthly stipend given monthly, including a scholarship funded by the Office of International Affairs and the matching funds from the student's college, department, or advisor
Tuition and credit fees: either fully waived, or charged according to the rates of local students
The tuition waiver covers basic tuition and credit fees only; incidental fees such as dormitories, insurance and campus facilities, and the summer semester, are not covered
application_method: Current NYCU students: apply and upload the required documents in the NYCU scholarship application system during the Fall Semester (January 15-March 15) or Spring Semester (July 15-September 15) window

Incoming students: mark 'Apply for NYCU Scholarship' in the scholarship section of the online admission application and submit it together with the admission documents; the result is listed in the admission letter
official.application_route: Current students apply through the NYCU scholarship application system inside the January 15-March 15 or July 15-September 15 windows; incoming students tick the scholarship option inside the online admission application.
official.citizenship_residency: Foreign-national degree students admitted under Taiwan's Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan; awardees must present an Alien Residence Certificate, and an ARC granted for work reasons disqualifies the applicant.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is exclusively for international (foreign-national) degree students at NYCU.
official.research_requirement: Master's and Ph.D. applicants who have met graduation credit requirements and therefore have no course grades must attach a research proposal or thesis/dissertation description.
official.duration: Approved for 1 year at a time; maximum award duration 4 years for undergraduate students (set by each department's regulated study period), 2 years for master's students, 5 years for Ph.D. students, and up to 6 years for students who directly pursue a Ph.D.
official.description: NYCU provides scholarship opportunities for international students pursuing degrees: monthly stipends and tuition awards that may be granted together or separately, decided by department, college and university committee review. The stipend combines an Office of International Affairs scholarship with matching funds from the student's college, department or advisor.
official.program_type: University (institutional) scholarship for international degree students

verification.notes: All facts verified on the awarding body's own pages: the NYCU OIA University Scholarships page (EN and CH versions), the OIA International Students Scholarships FAQ, and the official NYCU International Student Scholarship Guidelines PDF linked from that page. The monthly stipend amount for this scholarship is deliberately not published: the guidelines state that numbers and amounts are flexibly adjusted based on budgetary considerations and that stipend standards are stipulated by the International Scholarships and Grants Committee. The NT$33,000 per month figure published on the same page belongs to the separate Elite Ph.D. Scholarship, not this award, and was therefore excluded. Deadlines are published as recurring annual windows rather than a single dated deadline; no English test requirement or study mode is stated for the scholarship itself.

applicant_utility.summary: NYCU's International Student Scholarship pairs a monthly stipend - part university funding, part matching money from your college, department or advisor - with either a full waiver of tuition and credit fees or local-student tuition rates, and the two components can be awarded together or separately. Because the stipend level is set year by year by the university's International Scholarships and Grants Committee against the budget, no figure is published anywhere, so treat the stipend as variable and line up an advisor's matching-fund commitment before you apply. Current students must file inside one of two hard windows each year (January 15-March 15 or July 15-September 15), while incoming applicants only tick the scholarship box in the online admission form and receive the outcome in the admission letter. Keeping the award means holding a 3.5 (graduate) or 3.0 (undergraduate) average and an A conduct grade, filing transcripts and tuition receipts every semester, and completing the Mandarin course quota before graduation.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-GPA international students already at or admitted to NYCU who hold no Taiwan government scholarship and whose advisor or department can commit matching funds.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold no Taiwan government scholarship or grant (MOE Taiwan Scholarship, MOFA, ICDF) - concurrent receipt is barred except for specially approved programs
Secure your advisor's agreement to the matching funds before the window opens, since the stipend combines OIA money with college, department or advisor matching

Assemble the file: application form, full academic-year transcripts, an A-or-above conduct grade record, the advisor's recommendation letter, and a research proposal or thesis description if you have no course grades
Incoming applicants: mark 'Apply for NYCU Scholarship' in the scholarship section of the online admission application instead of applying separately
Get your ARC and open a Taiwan Post Office account early - the stipend is paid only into a Post Office account, and new students typically wait 6-8 weeks for the first deposit
Book the Mandarin load into your study plan from semester one: 4 courses for undergraduates and 2 for graduate students, waivable with TOCFL Level 2+ or the NYCU placement test
common_rejection_risks: Filing outside the two fixed annual windows - late application documents are explicitly not accepted
Holding or later accepting a Taiwan government scholarship, which disqualifies you from this award
No advisor, department or college matching-fund commitment behind the stipend application
Cumulative GPA drifting under 3.5 (graduate) or 3.0 (undergraduate), or a conduct grade below A, at review or renewal
Skipping the every-semester transcript and tuition-payment-receipt submission, which cuts off the next semester's payment
Assuming strong grades guarantee the award - allocation still depends on committee review and the annual budget
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Airfare to Taiwan, accommodation, insurance and campus facility fees (the waiver covers basic tuition and credit fees only, excluding the summer semester), any tuition balance when the award is the local-student rate rather than a full waiver, and living costs above the unpublished, budget-set monthly stipend.
document_audit: Transcripts must cover the full academic year; students with only one semester completed are judged on that single semester
The conduct grade (A or above, each semester) is a separate mandatory item from academic transcripts
An advisor recommendation letter is required, not optional, for the existing-student scholarship
Tuition payment receipts are needed every semester after the award, not just at application time
An ARC issued for work reasons blocks the scholarship entirely; dependents and APRC holders must sign a no-full-time-work undertaking
TOCFL Level 2+ certificates or NYCU Chinese Language Center placement-test passes are the accepted proofs for waiving the Mandarin quota
alerts: Two windows a year only - January 15-March 15 (Fall) and July 15-September 15 (Spring); nothing is accepted in between
The stipend amount is unpublished and budget-dependent: do not budget from the NT$33,000 Elite Ph.D. figure on the same page, which is a different, college-recommended scheme
Awards run one year at a time with hard ceilings of 2 years (master's) and 5 years (Ph.D.); beyond that only the local tuition rate may be available
Stipends land around the 10th of each month except January and the first month of each semester, and the first payment can take 6-8 weeks after registration
Leaving campus for more than 30 days without written advisor approval, or graduating, suspending or dropping out, suspends payment immediately
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You file in the NYCU scholarship application system (or inside the admission application), the department screens, the college ranks the candidates, and the International Scholarships and Grants Committee decides; new students see the result in the admission letter and awards are renewed one year at a time.
